## Description
 For a 1m × 1m board XPS (Extruded Polystyrene). Density 35 kg/m³. Each 5.25 kg&#10;&#9;&#9;  It is extremely lightweight compared to the other materials. For reference, a 100 mm &#10;&#9;&#9;  polycarbonate sheet of the same area would weigh ~25 kg (55 lbs), roughly 8–16× more.&#10;&#9;&#9;  &#10;&#9;&#9;  XPS is made from polystyrene (PS), which is produced by free-radical addition &#10;&#9;&#9;  polymerization of the monomer styrene (vinylbenzene, C₈H₈):&#10;&#9;&#9;  &#10;&#9;&#9;  XPS is made in a continuous extrusion line with these stages:&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;1. Raw material feeding – Polystyrene (PS) resin pellets (crystalline form) are blended &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   with additives: flame retardant, nucleating agent, pigment, and combustion aid in a &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   high-intensity mixer. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2. Primary extrusion (plasticizing) – The blend is fed into a twin-screw extruder &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   where heat (electrical + shear) melts the PS crystals into a homogeneous viscous &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   melt at ~200–230 °C. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;3. Blowing agent injection – CO₂ (most common today) or HFC gas is injected under high &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   pressure into the molten PS in a secondary extruder.  The gas is held dissolved in &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   the melt by pressure. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;4. Extrusion through slot die – The pressurized, gas-loaded melt is forced through a &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   wide slot die.  As it exits, pressure drops sharply → the dissolved gas expands &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   rapidly, nucleating thousands of tiny closed cells per mm³. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;5. Calibration and cooling – The expanding foam is drawn through a calibrating frame &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   (mandrel) that sets the exact thickness and width, while chilled water solidifies &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   the cell walls.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;6. Haul-off, trimming, and cutting – The continuous board is pulled at constant speed, &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   edges are trimmed (ship-lap profile), and the board is cross-cut to length &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   (typically 2.4 m). &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;7. Stacking and packaging. The result is a uniform closed-cell foam — this is what &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   makes XPS more moisture-resistant and stronger than EPS (which has fused-bead &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   interstitial voids).&#10;&#9;&#9;
